subject: Transportation Systems
title: The Rise of the Automobile
description: A fast breakdown of The Rise of the Automobile for builders.

hook.text: Ford's Model T cost $260 in 1925. Suddenly, ordinary families could travel wherever they wanted.

buildup.text: Cars offered door-to-door travel with no schedules, no tickets, and total freedom.

discovery.text: Governments poured money into highways. Railway funding shriveled. The balance tipped fast.

twist.text: America had 254,000 miles of rail in 1916. By 1970, nearly half had been abandoned.

climax.text: The car killed the passenger train in America. Freight survived, but riders vanished.

punchline.text: Freedom on four wheels emptied the stations.

quiz.question: What made cars a serious threat to passenger rail?
